text:
alice: quick question — customer hit truncated JSON from SSE when client paused for ~200ms (gc) then retried. looks like two partial objects got stitched and parse failed. do our SDKs try to drain the buffer before reconnect, or do they just re-open and keep the partial bytes?
ben: we currently re-open and append new bytes to the stream buffer in node/go clients, which can produce concatenated partial JSON if chunk boundary lands mid-object. not draining atm.
carla: that explains the failures i saw in the python repro. i was seeing `{"id":1,"text":"hello` then next connect sent ` world"}{"id":2...` => JSON error.
dave: for backpressure+pause scenario we should probably do one of: 1) drain/emit partial objects only on valid parse boundaries 2) on reconnect, discard trailing partial chunk and request replay from server with offset/token 3) include a small per-connection seq header so server can dedupe.
elena: option 2 sounds safest for strong correctness — drop trailing partial and ask server for replay from last acked token. but client needs to surface a stable resume token.
alice: suggestion: add a `resume_token` in the SSE meta events and SDK-level `resume_on_connect: true|false` flag. if true, SDK will drop trailing incomplete bytes and call /events?resume=<token>.
ben: implementation notes for node SDK: currently parser is streaming-line-based then ndjson JSON.parse on each line. for partial json we can keep a tail buffer until parse succeeds. but with reconnect we need a policy: either preserve tail (risk duplicate partials) or drop tail and request resume token.
carla: mini repro i ran in python — i put a delay and forced reconnect. logs: `BUFFER TAIL=\"{\"id\":1,\"text\":\"hello\"` then `NEW CHUNK=\" world\"}`. parser tried to splice and failed.
dave: short-term patch: treat backpressure pause > X ms as a disconnect that triggers a resume flow (i.e., drop tail and request replay). X maybe 100ms by default.
elena: for Dedicated/private we should add server-side support: emit checkpoint events every N characters: `event: checkpoint
data: {"token":"tok_abc","offset":12345}` so SDK can resume cleanly.
alice: can we add a header `x-sse-graceful-drain: true` that tells proxy to wait up to 100ms for client buffer flush before forcibly reconnecting? might help platform-managed clients.
b en: small nit — multi-language clients have different buffer semantics. Go reader uses io.Reader streaming and tends to hand bytes to decoder ASAP. Node uses streams + string slicing. We need per-sdk tweaks.
carla: I'll open a tiny design PR proposing: 1) resume_token metadata event, 2) SDK flag `resume_on_reconnect`, 3) default behaviour: drop tail and resume.
dave: +1. also add a non-breaking server config to emit checkpoints (opt-in for legacy).
elena: for observability, add a metric `sse.partial_replays` and a debug log when we drop tail + resume token used.
deploy-bot: note: rolling feature flag gate requested by @carla — enable checkpoint events behind `sse.checkpoints` feature flag.
alice: action items: @carla open PR for spec + feature flag, @ben add node client `resume_on_reconnect` and tail-drop fallback, @dave add server checkpoint event support, @elena add metric + logs. I'll file an issue linking this thread. thanks :thumbsup:
ben: quick question on config shape — propose in node client config:
```js
{
  resume_on_reconnect: true,
  resume_timeout_ms: 100, // time to wait before treating pause as disconnect
  max_tail_bytes: 64 * 1024 // drop if tail smaller than this, else error
}
```
carla: LGTM. for go client similar fields with `ResumeOnReconnect bool` and `ResumeTimeout time.Duration`.
dave: let's also add an integration test that injects GC-like pause and verifies no parse errors across languages.
elena: noted. i'll add dashboards for partial_replays and a small alert when rate > 1/min for a customer.
alice: perfect. i'll follow up with the issue + link to this thread. thanks everyone.
